sentences.zh: 你好，各位美丽的极客们。
我有一个重大消息要宣布。

sentences.en: After 10 years of being an independent production, with our 10th year probably being our biggest ever, putting out three special project spinoffs and a bestselling book,
sentences.zh: 在独立制作了十年，且第十年可能是我们有史以来最辉煌的一年，不仅推出了三个特别衍生项目，还出版了一本畅销书之后，

sentences.en: I've decided to sell the show to Sirius XM, specifically to Stitcher, which is their podcast company.
sentences.zh: 我决定将这档节目卖给 Sirius XM，具体来说是卖给他们的播客公司 Stitcher。

sentences.en: The same 99PI crew are going to make the show.
sentences.zh: 99PI 原班人马将继续制作这档节目。

sentences.en: I'm still going to host it.

sentences.zh: 我们仍保持独立的编辑团队。

sentences.en: It'll still be available anywhere to everyone.
sentences.zh: 节目依然会面向所有人，在任何平台都能收听。

sentences.en: If you're subscribed now, you will stay subscribed.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在已经订阅了，你将继续保持订阅状态。
节目内容不会有任何改变。

sentences.en: Someone else just collects the ad money and guides the business stuff.
sentences.zh: 只是换了人来收取广告费并指导商业运作。

sentences.en: You'll never notice the sound of anything different, except I get to be involved more.
sentences.zh: 除了我能更多地参与其中之外，你绝不会察觉到任何声音上的不同。

sentences.en: So much of my job has become running a business and not making a podcaSt. I desperately needed that to change.
sentences.zh: 我的工作中有太多时间花在经营公司上，而不是制作播客。我迫切需要改变这种状况。

sentences.en: I chose Stitcher as my new partner because I already knew, trusted, and respected everyone there.
sentences.zh: 我选择 Stitcher 作为新合作伙伴，是因为我了解、信任并尊重那里的每一个人。

sentences.en: The ball got rolling when I called Colin Anderson.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于我给 Colin Anderson 打的那通电话。

sentences.en: He's the VP of Comedy at Earwolf.
sentences.zh: 他是 Earwolf 喜剧部门的副总裁。

sentences.en: I literally signed his paperwork a decade ago for him to work in this country.
sentences.zh: 十年前，我甚至亲手签过他的工作许可文件，让他能在这个国家工作。

sentences.en: He was on furlough from the comedy production group at BBC Radio, and I signed the paperwork for him to work at KLW in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 当时他正从 BBC 电台的喜剧制作组休假，我签了文件让他去旧金山的 KLW 工作。

sentences.en: And then he hooked me up with Natalie Moellum, the VP of Business Development, and she and I hit it off right away because she also happens to be the sister of John Moellum,
sentences.zh: 后来他把我介绍给了业务发展副总裁 Natalie Moellum，我们一见如故，因为她恰好是 John Moellum 的妹妹，

sentences.en: who wrote and performed the amazing song-story collaborations, Wild Ones and Genie Chance, which are like our best episodes ever.
sentences.zh: John 创作并表演了那些精彩的歌曲故事合作项目《Wild Ones》和《Genie Chance》，那简直是我们有史以来最棒的剧集。

sentences.en: So talking to her was like talking to a cousin.
sentences.zh: 所以和她交谈就像在和亲戚聊天一样。

sentences.en: And the person who will be my boss is Peter Clowney.
sentences.zh: 而我未来的老板是 Peter Clowney。

sentences.en: He's the head of original content at Stitcher.
sentences.zh: 他是 Stitcher 原创内容部门的负责人。

sentences.en: And he was my editor 15 years ago.
sentences.zh: 他曾是我 15 年前的编辑。

sentences.en: We worked on pilots for public radio, and it's safe to say that if Peter hadn't been my editor then, 99% Invisible wouldn't exist today.
sentences.zh: 我们曾一起制作过公共广播的试播集，可以肯定地说，如果当时没有 Peter 做我的编辑，今天就不会有《99% Invisible》。

sentences.en: Then I met a bunch of the serious folks, and a lot of them had never heard of the show before, but by the end of our negotiations,
sentences.zh: 后来我见了一些 Stitcher 的核心成员，他们中很多人之前从未听说过这档节目，但在谈判结束时，

sentences.en: they had heartfelt and insightful comments about episodes deep in the back catalog that I barely remembered.
sentences.zh: 他们对那些我几乎快要遗忘的早期剧集发表了发自肺腑且深刻的见解。

sentences.en: And you would like them too, but you'll never notice them.
sentences.zh: 你们也会喜欢他们的，尽管你们永远不会注意到他们的存在。
他们只是让我感到安心。

sentences.en: So what's going to happen with Radiotopia?
sentences.zh: 那么 Radiotopia 会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: I am so proud of the things that PRX CEO Kerry Hoffman, executive producer Julie Shapiro, network director Audrey Martovich, and fundraiser Gina James,
sentences.zh: 我为 PRX 首席执行官 Kerry Hoffman、执行制片人 Julie Shapiro、网络总监 Audrey Martovich 和筹款人 Gina James 所取得的成就感到无比自豪，

sentences.en: and all the rest of the behind-the-scenes crew built with Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: 以及所有与 Radiotopia 一起奋斗的幕后团队。

sentences.en: It became more successful than I ever imagined when we dreamed it up in a cabin in rural Massachusetts several years ago.
sentences.zh: 它比我们几年前在马萨诸塞州乡村的小木屋里构想时所预想的还要成功。

sentences.en: I raised money and worked side-by-side with amazing podcasters, each of them retaining ownership and control over their own work.
sentences.zh: 我筹集了资金，并与出色的播客制作人们并肩工作，他们每个人都保留了对自己作品的所有权和控制权。

sentences.en: Radiotopia is a groundbreaking network and nonprofit collective.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia 是一个开创性的网络和非营利性集体。

sentences.en: It has never been a company on purpose, and as such, even though I was the co-founder, I never owned any part of it.
sentences.zh: 它从一开始就不是以公司形式存在的，因此，尽管我是联合创始人，但我从未拥有过它的任何股份。

sentences.en: I think that was so weird to people that no one really understood it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这对人们来说太奇怪了，以至于没人能真正理解。

sentences.en: I still believe in the ongoing mission of Radiotopia and the amazing work of PRX on the forefront of public radio, and I hope you continue to support them.
sentences.zh: 我依然坚信 Radiotopia 的持续使命，以及 PRX 在公共广播前沿所做的出色工作，希望你们能继续支持他们。

sentences.en: I'm personally donating a million dollars to PRX and Radiotopia so they keep going strong.
sentences.zh: 我个人将向 PRX 和 Radiotopia 捐赠一百万美元，以确保他们继续稳步前行。

sentences.en: Whatever cliche you have in mind about what happens in an acquisition when shows move to other networks, this isn't like that.
sentences.zh: 无论你对节目被收购并转投其他网络有什么刻板印象，这次的情况完全不同。

sentences.en: A bunch of people from the PRX and Sirius teams worked together with good intentions to transform a show that needed to evolve for the sake of its creator,
sentences.zh: PRX 和 Sirius 团队的许多人怀着善意共同努力，为了创作者的未来，对一档需要进化的节目进行了转型，

sentences.en: and I am grateful for that.
And I'm grateful to you for listening.
99% Invisible will keep on and grow, and the team will have even more opportunities to make more stuff and spinoffs with the full support of Stitcher and SiriusXM.
sentences.zh: 《99% Invisible》将继续前行并不断成长，在 Stitcher 和 SiriusXM 的全力支持下，团队将有更多机会制作更多内容和衍生项目。

sentences.en: I'm really excited to collaborate in ways I never imagined.
sentences.zh: 我非常期待以我从未想象过的方式进行合作。

sentences.en: So thank you, beautiful nerds, for getting us here, and thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 所以，感谢你们，美丽的极客们，是你们让我们走到了今天，感谢你们的收听。

sentences.en: We were all extremely busy the past couple of weeks, so right now I'm going to play for you a repeat, which is hosted by Delaney Hall, but nothing should be read into that.
sentences.zh: 过去几周我们都非常忙碌，所以现在我将为大家重播一期节目，由 Delaney Hall 主持，但这并不代表什么特殊含义。

sentences.en: This one just happens to be one of my favorite episodes, probably because it was hosted by Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 这期节目恰好是我最喜欢的剧集之一，大概是因为它是由 Delaney Hall 主持的。

sentences.en: I'm Delaney Hall, filling in for Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是 Delaney Hall，代班 Roman Mars。

sentences.en: In 1997, a curator named Catherine Ott was learning her way around the Smithsonian National Museum of American History.
sentences.zh: 1997 年，一位名叫 Catherine Ott 的策展人正在熟悉史密森尼国家美国历史博物馆的环境。

sentences.en: She was new to the job, she specialized in medical science, and there was this one storage room in the building where she worked.
sentences.zh: 她刚入职，专攻医学科学，她工作的大楼里有一个储藏室。

sentences.en: It's like that classic, what you'd think of as a dark, dusty, sort of scary, mildly mysterious storage room in a museum.
sentences.zh: 就像你想象中博物馆里那种昏暗、尘土飞扬、有点吓人、又带点神秘感的储藏室。

sentences.en: There were drug jars, there was parts of mannequin bodies laying around.
sentences.zh: 里面有药罐，还有散落的人体模型部件。

sentences.en: There was this wheelchair that had go-kart wheels.
sentences.zh: 有一把装了卡丁车轮子的轮椅。

sentences.en: It had a Recaro seat that was used in Porsche cars.
sentences.zh: 它装了一个保时捷汽车上用的 Recaro 座椅。

sentences.en: But I kept tripping over it, and finally I'm like, what the heck is this thing?
sentences.zh: 但我总是被它绊倒，最后我心想，这到底是什么鬼东西？

sentences.en: So Catherine Ott started asking around, where did this wheelchair come from?
sentences.zh: 于是 Catherine Ott 开始四处打听，这把轮椅是从哪来的？
为什么它会在储藏室里？

sentences.en: And no one at the castle, which is what the staff calls the main Smithsonian building, could really tell her.
sentences.zh: 但城堡里（员工对史密森尼主楼的称呼）没人能说清楚。

sentences.en: Nobody completely understood who had owned it.
sentences.zh: 没人完全知道它曾经的主人是谁。

sentences.en: It had been left at the door of the castle with a note pinned to it, like an orphan, in a basket.
sentences.zh: 它就像一个被遗弃在篮子里的孤儿，被留在了城堡的门口，上面还别着一张纸条。

sentences.en: And the note said, this was a chair that belonged to Ed Roberts.
sentences.zh: 纸条上写着：这是一把属于 Ed Roberts 的椅子。

sentences.en: We think it should be at the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 我们认为它应该被史密森尼博物馆收藏。

sentences.en: If you live in an American city and you don't personally use a wheelchair,
sentences.zh: 如果你住在美国城市，且平时不用轮椅，

sentences.en: you probably don't pay much attention to the small slope at most intersections between the sidewalk and the street.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会注意到大多数路口人行道和街道之间那个小小的斜坡。

sentences.en: It's just a ramp, a cut in the curb.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个坡道，路缘石上的一个切口。

sentences.en: They're all over the country now, just about any place you find sidewalks.
sentences.zh: 现在全国各地到处都是，几乎只要有人行道的地方就有。

sentences.en: But 60 years ago, when Ed Roberts, the owner of that wheelchair, was young,
sentences.zh: 但在 60 年前，当那把轮椅的主人 Ed Roberts 还年轻的时候，

sentences.en: the sidewalks at most urban intersections ended with a sharp drop-off.
sentences.zh: 大多数城市路口的人行道尽头都是陡峭的落差。

sentences.en: That's enough to stop a person in a wheelchair from reaching the next block without help.
sentences.zh: 这足以让坐轮椅的人在没有帮助的情况下无法到达下一个街区。

sentences.en: And the story of how the first widespread urban curb cuts came to be,
sentences.zh: 而关于这种广泛的城市路缘坡道是如何出现的，

sentences.en: it starts with a movement that demanded society see disabled people in a new way.
sentences.zh: 始于一场要求社会以全新视角看待残疾人的运动。

sentences.en: Ed Roberts was central to that movement,
sentences.zh: Ed Roberts 是这场运动的核心人物，

sentences.en: and so were the hundreds of people who helped drag his wheelchair up Constitution Avenue
sentences.zh: 还有数百人帮忙把他的轮椅拖上宪法大道，

sentences.en: right in the middle of Washington, D.C., so it could end up at the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 就在华盛顿特区的中心地带，这样它最终才能进入史密森尼博物馆。

sentences.en: They insisted it was a piece of American history.
sentences.zh: 他们坚持认为这是一段美国历史。

sentences.en: Ed Roberts grew up in Burlingame, near San Francisco.
sentences.zh: Ed Roberts 在旧金山附近的伯林格姆长大。

sentences.en: He was the oldest of four boys, and he loved to play baseball.
sentences.zh: 他是四个男孩中的老大，热爱打棒球。

sentences.en: But one day, when he was 14 years old, he got really sick with a fever.
sentences.zh: 但在他 14 岁那年的一天，他因为高烧病得很重。

sentences.en: Within a few days, he was in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 几天之内，他就住进了医院。
那是 Ed 的母亲 Zona Roberts。

sentences.en: And within two days of that, he was in, rushed to an iron lung,
sentences.zh: 两天之内，他就被紧急送进了铁肺呼吸机，

sentences.en: because he couldn't breathe anymore on his own.
sentences.zh: 因为他已经无法自主呼吸了。
Ed 患上了小儿麻痹症。

sentences.en: It had damaged his respiratory muscles so much that he needed the iron lung to stay alive.
sentences.zh: 它严重损害了他的呼吸肌，以至于他必须依靠铁肺才能活下去。

sentences.en: Iron lungs aren't made anymore, but back in the day,
sentences.zh: 现在已经不再生产铁肺了，但在那个年代，

sentences.en: they were these full-body respirators that encased polio survivors in metal up to the neck
sentences.zh: 它们是那种全身式的呼吸器，将小儿麻痹症幸存者从脖子以下包裹在金属中，

sentences.en: and pulled air in and out of their lungs.
sentences.zh: 通过压力将空气泵入和泵出他们的肺部。

sentences.en: Ed's polio wrecked a lot more than his breathing.
sentences.zh: Ed 的小儿麻痹症摧毁的不仅仅是他的呼吸功能。

sentences.en: It left him paralyzed below the neck.
sentences.zh: 它导致他脖子以下瘫痪。

sentences.en: He could move two fingers on his left hand, and that was it.
sentences.zh: 他左手的两根手指能动，仅此而已。

sentences.en: The doctor who told Ed's parents their son had survived his high fever
sentences.zh: 那位告诉 Ed 的父母他们的儿子挺过了高烧的医生，

sentences.en: did not present this as good news.
sentences.zh: 并没有把这当作好消息。

sentences.en: He said, well, how would you feel if you had to live in an iron lung the rest of your life?
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，如果你们余生都必须住在铁肺里，你们会怎么想？

sentences.en: I don't imagine you've ever been in one.
sentences.zh: 我想你们从来没住过那种东西。

sentences.en: I've been in one, and it's not a very good way to live.
sentences.zh: 我住过，那可不是什么好的生活方式。

sentences.en: In order to escape the iron lung once in a while,
Ed taught himself on his own a technique called frog breathing.
sentences.zh: Ed 自学了一种叫“青蛙呼吸法”的技巧。

sentences.en: That's a deep sea diver's trick where you gulp oxygen into your lungs the way a frog does.
sentences.zh: 那是深海潜水员的一种技巧，像青蛙一样把氧气吞进肺里。

sentences.en: For polio survivors whose weakened breathing muscles weren't strong enough to inhale that needed oxygen,
sentences.zh: 对于那些呼吸肌虚弱、无法吸入足够氧气的小儿麻痹症幸存者来说，

sentences.en: and frog breathing meant a person could get out of the iron lung for short stretches of time.
sentences.zh: 青蛙呼吸法意味着他们可以短时间离开铁肺。

sentences.en: You swallow it, and then you can breathe.
sentences.zh: 吞下去，然后你就能呼吸了。

sentences.en: And they kept telling him to stop it.
sentences.zh: 他们一直叫他停止这样做。

sentences.en: That was not good for his body, and of course he kept doing it because it kept him alive.
sentences.zh: 这对他的身体不好，但他当然坚持这样做，因为这能让他活下去。

sentences.en: And Ed was determined to stay alive on his own terMs.
sentences.zh: Ed 决心按照自己的方式活下去。

sentences.en: Here he is in a 60 Minutes interview from 1989.
sentences.zh: 这是他在 1989 年接受《60 分钟》采访时的片段。

sentences.en: There are very few people, even with the most severe disabilities, who can't take control of their own life.
sentences.zh: 很少有人，即使是残疾程度最严重的人，不能掌控自己的生活。

sentences.en: The problem is that people around us don't expect this to.
sentences.zh: 问题在于周围的人并不指望他们能做到。

sentences.en: If you had people taking care of you, making all your decisions, what is there to life?
sentences.zh: 如果有人照顾你，替你做所有的决定，那生活还有什么意义？

sentences.en: Ed was tenacious, but everything was hard.
sentences.zh: Ed 很顽强，但一切都很艰难。

sentences.en: He needed the iron lung while he was asleep, but the frog breathing let him leave it for a while during the day.
sentences.zh: 他睡觉时需要铁肺，但青蛙呼吸法让他白天可以离开它一会儿。

sentences.en: So he stayed in school, going to campus once a week.
sentences.zh: 所以他坚持上学，每周去一次校园。

sentences.en: When Ed did leave the house, his family ran the maneuvers.
sentences.zh: 当 Ed 离开家时，他的家人负责操作这些动作。

sentences.en: They were helping him navigate a world that wasn't built for a person in a wheelchair.
sentences.zh: 他们帮他在一个并非为轮椅使用者建造的世界里穿行。

sentences.en: Ed's brothers or his dad would help lift him into his chair, drag the chair out of the house,
sentences.zh: Ed 的兄弟或父亲会帮他抬上轮椅，把椅子拖出房子，

sentences.en: and then lift the chair over curbs and up and down stairs.
sentences.zh: 然后把椅子抬过路缘石，上下楼梯。

sentences.en: Or if Zona were alone, she would wrangle strangers.
sentences.zh: 或者如果 Zona 一个人，她就会找陌生人帮忙。

sentences.en: I'd have to get somebody to help me get the chair up the stairs.
sentences.zh: 我得找人帮我把椅子抬上楼梯。

sentences.en: So it would be somebody in the back and somebody on the frame and get it up.
sentences.zh: 一个人在后面，一个人抬着框架，把它抬上去。

sentences.en: Or sometimes it would just be me.
sentences.zh: 或者有时候就只有我一个人。

sentences.en: Ed graduated from high school, then from a local community college.
sentences.zh: Ed 从高中毕业，然后又从当地的社区学院毕业。

sentences.en: But when he wanted to go on to Berkeley in 1962, the university at first said no.
sentences.zh: 但当他 1962 年想去伯克利分校深造时，大学起初拒绝了。

sentences.en: And where could he safely live?
sentences.zh: 而且他能安全住在哪里呢？

sentences.en: The iron lung, which he still used every night, wouldn't fit in a dorm room.
sentences.zh: 他每晚都要用的铁肺根本放不进宿舍。

sentences.en: Until finally somebody suggested housing him at the campus hospital.
sentences.zh: 直到最后有人建议让他住在校园医院。

sentences.en: A patient's room remade into a living space for Ed and all his equipment.
sentences.zh: 把病房改造成 Ed 和他所有设备的居住空间。

sentences.en: This is Ed Roberts, side two, tape one, September 15th.
sentences.zh: 这是 Ed Roberts，第二面，第一盘磁带，9 月 15 日。

sentences.en: In a series of oral history interviews much later, Ed remembered what it was like to start as a Berkeley undergrad.
sentences.zh: 在后来的一系列口述历史访谈中，Ed 回忆了作为伯克利本科生开始学习时的情景。

sentences.en: Do you remember the day you moved in the couch?
sentences.zh: 你还记得你搬进宿舍的那天吗？

sentences.en: It was a combination of excitement and scary, Ed.
sentences.zh: 那是一种既兴奋又害怕的感觉，Ed。

sentences.en: An attendant would wheel Ed to each class.
sentences.zh: 会有护理人员推着埃德去上每一堂课。

sentences.en: And then Ed would recruit a classmate to help him take notes.
sentences.zh: 然后埃德会招募一名同学帮他记笔记。

sentences.en: And then I'd start making an announcement at the beginning of class.
sentences.zh: 我会在课前开始做个公告。

sentences.en: And usually find a good-looking young woman.
sentences.zh: 通常会找一位长相好看的年轻女性。

sentences.en: He'd give the woman a piece of carbon paper.
sentences.zh: 他会给那位女士一张复写纸。

sentences.en: She would take notes during the lecture.
sentences.zh: 她会在讲座期间记笔记。

sentences.en: And then she'd give the carbon copy back to Ed at the end.
sentences.zh: 课后她会把复写件交给埃德。

sentences.en: It's such a simple way to take notes.
